observations.why: Imperative verb directed at an audience enacts command hierarchy — speaker positions as one entitled to direct what others retain or discard.
Direct imperative to eliminate shared knowledge enacts authority-ranking: the speaker commands erasure of information others hold.
Speaker asserts a definitive institutional record to override and nullify what others may believe, enacting authority-ranking through epistemic authority rather than command form.

mints.name: DirectiveKnowledgeErasure
mints.title: Remove all knowledge
mints.frame: Is the speaker commanding the elimination of what others know or believe, positioning authority over shared epistemic state?
